skill.name: labarchive-integration
skill.description: Automate LabArchives notebook access, backups, entries, attachments, reports, and documented integrations through the LabArchives API.
skill.summary: Manage LabArchives electronic lab notebooks with reusable Python scripts and API guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, identifiers, documentation examples, and expected LabArchives API access. Confirmed risks involve credential-bearing requests, disabled TLS verification guidance, and plaintext credential storage; semantic review also found echoed password input, unchecked custom endpoints, and unpinned installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Password prompts use visible terminal input.
remediation.suggestion: Use getpass.getpass for both password fields and avoid printing secret values.

remediation.issue: The setup script stores institutional and user credentials in plaintext YAML.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a system secret store or environment variables. If a file is required, create it atomically with mode 0600.

remediation.issue: A custom API endpoint can receive all configured credentials without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS, validate official domains by default, and display an explicit warning before sending credentials to custom hosts.

remediation.issue: Authentication guidance shows TLS certificate verification disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Remove verify=False guidance or require a trusted custom CA bundle for test environments.

remediation.issue: Installation guidance fetches an unpinned third-party repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed release or commit and provide integrity verification for the installed dependency.

semantic_findings.title: Password Prompts Echo Secrets
semantic_findings.description: The setup script reads both password values with input(), so terminals and session recordings can display the secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both access_password and user_password are collected through Python input() rather than getpass, which visibly echoes typed values.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked Custom Endpoint Receives Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The setup accepts any custom URL and later initializes an authenticated client with it, allowing secrets to reach an unintended or insecure host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The custom endpoint is accepted without scheme or hostname checks and is passed directly to the client before credential-bearing authentication.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party Installation
semantic_findings.description: The guidance clones and installs the current state of a third-party repository without a release, commit, or integrity check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installation paths fetch a mutable Git repository reference, creating a clear dependency supply-chain risk.

content.value_statement: Manual LabArchives API work makes notebook backups, entries, and integrations slow and error-prone. This skill provides scripts and references for authenticated notebook automation.
actual_capabilities: Configure regional LabArchives API endpoints and credentials in a protected YAML file.
Authenticate a user and retrieve the user identifier required by API operations.
List accessible notebooks and save full or metadata-only notebook backups.
Create notebook entries and add comments through the LabArchives API.
Upload one attachment or every file from a selected directory.
Provide documented patterns for Jupyter, Protocols.io, REDCap, OAuth, and scientific software integrations.
limitations: An Enterprise LabArchives license, API access, and valid credentials are required.
The scripts depend on PyYAML, requests, and the third-party labarchives-py package.
Third-party integration examples are templates, not complete production connectors.
The skill does not encrypt configuration files or downloaded notebook backups.

use_cases.title: Back Up Research Notebooks
use_cases.description: List accessible notebooks and create local archives with optional attachment exclusion.

use_cases.title: Publish Experiment Results
use_cases.description: Create entries, add comments, and attach result files to a selected notebook.

use_cases.title: Design ELN Integrations
use_cases.description: Use API and OAuth examples to plan connections with analysis, protocol, or clinical systems.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which LabArchives regional endpoint matches [institution region]. List the credentials I need, but do not request their values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Notebook Backup
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a backup plan for notebook [notebook ID]. Use [output directory], include [attachments choice], and ask before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Entry Upload
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an entry titled [title] in notebook [notebook ID] with files from [path]. Confirm destinations and files before any upload.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reproducible Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LabArchives workflow for [source system]. Include authentication, data transformation, metadata, rate limits, validation, retries, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: List the information needed before backing up a notebook.
Plan a metadata-only backup for notebook 67890.
output_examples.output: The plan authenticates the configured user, confirms access to notebook 67890, requests JSON metadata without attachments, and saves it in the approved directory.
Run the notebook, export HTML, create a dated LabArchives entry, attach the original notebook, record environment metadata, and verify the upload.

best_practices: Use the official HTTPS endpoint for the institution and verify its hostname before authentication.
Keep credentials in a secret manager and protect downloaded notebooks according to research data policy.
Confirm notebook identifiers, file paths, and write operations before changing or exporting data.
anti_patterns: Do not disable TLS verification or send credentials to an unverified custom endpoint.
Do not commit config.yaml, credentials, or notebook backups to version control.
Do not bulk upload, overwrite configuration, or back up every notebook without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: What access does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Enterprise LabArchives API access, institutional API credentials, and a user external applications password.

faq.question: Which regions are supported?
faq.answer: The scripts include official endpoints for US and international, Australian, and United Kingdom LabArchives environments.

faq.question: Can it back up attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. Notebook backups include attachments by default, with options for metadata-only XML or JSON output.

faq.question: Can it create and update notebook content?
faq.answer: It can create entries, add comments, and upload attachments. The bundled script does not provide a general entry editing command.

faq.question: Are the third-party integrations complete?
faq.answer: No. The references provide workflows and code patterns that require adaptation, credentials, validation, and production testing.

faq.question: How should credentials and backups be protected?
faq.answer: Use a secret manager, official HTTPS endpoints, restrictive file permissions, encrypted storage, and approved research data handling procedures.
